score.sector: Healthcare / Biopharmaceuticals (rare endocrine diseases, TransCon platform)
score.moat_justification: TransCon prodrug platform validated by three approved rare-endocrine products (YORVIPATH — the only PTH replacement therapy for hypoparathyroidism; SKYTROFA weekly growth hormone; YUVIWEL for achondroplasia, approved Feb 2026) with specialty pricing power in the numbers: gross margin 83.4% (FY2023) → 87.8% (FY2024) → 86.8% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json. But there is no demonstrated return on capital: book equity is negative (-€162.8M at FY2025), the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is denominator noise (+180.6% in FY2019, -55.9% in FY2018, -3.0% in FY2025 despite an operating loss), and conservative owner's earnings are negative in 0 of the last 5 years. Revenue is concentrated (YORVIPATH ~80% of Q2 2026 product revenue), weekly-GH and PTH rivals are in market or in Phase 3, and SBC (€116.2M in FY2025) exceeds FY2025 free cash flow. A 5 gives CAP 8.5 years.

moat_for: TransCon platform validated across three approved products — YORVIPATH (only PTH replacement for hypoparathyroidism), SKYTROFA (once-weekly GH), YUVIWEL (achondroplasia, FDA-approved Feb 2026)
Specialty pricing power in the filed numbers: gross margin 83.4% (FY2023), 87.8% (FY2024), 86.8% (FY2025) as commercial mix scaled
Rare-disease commercial infrastructure: YORVIPATH available in 35+ countries, SKYTROFA >20,000 patients enrolled globally since launch
Platform monetization beyond own sales: Novo Nordisk license, Teijin Japan license (royalties up to mid-20s %), Eyconis ophthalmology spin-out with milestone/royalty rights
moat_against: No demonstrated returns on capital: owner's earnings negative 0/5 of the last 5 years, operating losses every filed year, book equity negative (-€162.8M at FY2025) so ROIC is not yet measurable, let alone above the cost of capital through a cycle
Single-product concentration: YORVIPATH ~80% of Q2 2026 product revenue (€252M of €315M)
Competition is real on both lead products: rival PTH therapy eneboparatide in Phase 3 (Amolyt/AstraZeneca), weekly-GH rivals (Novo Nordisk Sogroya, Pfizer/Opko NGENLA) against SKYTROFA

SBC is a heavy, recurring cost: €116.2M share-based payment in FY2025 (FY2024 €95.5M), exceeding FY2025 free cash flow; the EPS-note share count rose from 56,287,060 (FY2023) to 60,607,131 (FY2025) to fund the loss years
Finite patent/exclusivity horizons and rare-disease pricing politics cap how long the gross-margin structure can be assumed to persist

about.description_short: Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company focused on applying our innovative TransCon technology platform to make a meaningful difference for patients. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, and following our algorithm for product innovation, we apply TransCon to develop new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs. Ascendis is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, and has additional facilities in Europe and the United States. Please visit ascendispharma.com to learn more.

# ASND — Ascendis Pharma A/S
v5 run, 2026-10-17. **In scope** (market cap $13.652B at $225.25, nasdaq_quote_api — under the $40B scope cap). IFRS filer on Form 20-F (FY2025, filed 2026-02-11), reporting currency EUR, converted by the engine at period-end ECB rates. This run carries two filing overrides and the ADS-ratio declaration — see OVERRIDES.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.py output, or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Danish biopharma built on the TransCon prodrug platform, now a commercial rare-endocrine company: YORVIPATH (palopegteriparatide — the only parathyroid-hormone replacement therapy for adults with hypoparathyroidism), SKYTROFA (once-weekly growth hormone), and YUVIWEL (TransCon CNP for achondroplasia, FDA-approved February 2026). Plus platform licenses (Novo Nordisk, Teijin in Japan) and the Eyconis ophthalmology spin-out. One operating segment per the 20-F.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (20-F via EDGAR, USD as converted in financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $63,328,975 — the first positive OCF year in the history; capex $9,969,875 (by override, see below); SBC $136,500,925 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: -$83,141,825 = -$1.37/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $-1.37, latest FY OE total $-83.1M, shares 60,607,131). FCF was +$53,359,100; SBC alone consumed it 2.6 times over.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): **not computed** — the engine's D&A series is empty for this IFRS filer (da tag null in financials_history.csv), so oe_maintenance is blank. In words: the filed cash-flow statement does carry depreciation and amortization lines, but the engine did not capture them and no figure is recomputed here.
- OE positive **0 of the last 5** fiscal years. Per-year conservative OE/share (final run): FY2023 -$9.78, FY2024 -$7.03, FY2025 -$1.37 — improving fast, still negative.
- **Base used = the normalized 3-yr median: -$7.03/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). No TTM pin: ttm.py exits non-zero for this filer (it reads us-gaap taxonomies only — its error lists the ocf / sbc / shares legs as unavailable and capex as untagged), and the WORKER_SPEC rule for IFRS filers is the median base. The improving trajectory is handled in Thoughts, not by pinning a base the tools cannot produce.
- Balance sheet (latest FY, financials_history.csv): cash $723,848,175, total borrowings $957,207,875, **net debt $233.4M** (key_numbers.md; basis LongtermBorrowings+ShorttermBorrowings). Book equity is negative (-$191,314,675 converted; -€162.8M as filed) after a decade of losses.

## OVERRIDES — capex, shares, ADS ratio (all filing-sourced, all in bounds)
- **DATA_GAP (preliminary run, exit 4):** capex and shares, plus ADS_RATIO_MISSING. Preliminary base on filed data was -$7.21/share — the gaps were about tagging, not about the sign of the business.
- **capex_override = €8,485,000, kind "filing".** The filer reports PPE and intangible acquisitions on one combined cash-flow line, so no PPE-only tag exists for FY2024/FY2025. The combined line is an upper bound on PPE-only capex (conservative for OE). Basis proof: the FY2023 combined figure (€2,442k) is exactly the engine's last filed capex at the recorded ECB rate. The engine applied the single FY2025 value to both missing periods (USD fills in financials_history.csv: $8,815,067 for FY2024, $9,969,875 for FY2025) — it overstates FY2024's filed combined €1,427k by ~€7.1M, immaterial against FY2024 OCF of -€306.2M and conservative in direction. Out-of-band: false (last filed value €2,442,000).
- **shares_override = 60,607,131, kind "filing"** — the FY2025 20-F EPS note (Note 5) reports a single weighted-average count "for the purposes of basic and diluted earnings per share" (60,607,131 / 57,891,570 / 56,287,060 for FY2025/24/23), with basic and diluted EPS identical in all three years because the warrants, RSUs/PSUs and the convertible senior notes (3,456,785 shares on conversion) were excluded as antidilutive in loss years. The filer's diluted denominator therefore IS this count. The engine applied the FY2025 value to every missing period (2018–2025): for FY2023/FY2024 that is a larger denominator than the filer's own counts, shrinking the negative OE/share toward zero — against a harsher verdict, and the base stays deeply negative on either basis. Out-of-band: false.
- **ads_ratio = 1** — the 20-F cover page registers ADSs each representing one ordinary share. No scaling. (Post-period: in April 2026 the ADSs were mandatorily exchanged 1-for-1 into ordinary shares directly listed on Nasdaq under ASND, so the traded price is now per ordinary share in any case.)
- **Measured impact (key_numbers.md, overrides toggled in the same configuration):** base OE/share -$7.21 (no overrides) → **-$7.03** (with overrides), -2.46%. Unblocks tier: YES — without the overrides the filing gaps block scoring entirely.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, platform real, economics unproven
Justification: TransCon prodrug platform validated by three approved rare-endocrine products (YORVIPATH — the only PTH replacement therapy for hypoparathyroidism; SKYTROFA weekly growth hormone; YUVIWEL for achondroplasia, approved Feb 2026) with specialty pricing power in the numbers: gross margin 83.4% (FY2023) → 87.8% (FY2024) → 86.8% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json. But there is no demonstrated return on capital: book equity is negative (-€162.8M at FY2025), the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is denominator noise (+180.6% in FY2019, -55.9% in FY2018, -3.0% in FY2025 despite an operating loss), and conservative owner's earnings are negative in 0 of the last 5 years. Revenue is concentrated (YORVIPATH ~80% of Q2 2026 product revenue), weekly-GH and PTH rivals are in market or in Phase 3, and SBC (€116.2M in FY2025) exceeds FY2025 free cash flow.
- FOR: TransCon platform validated across three approved products; specialty pricing power (gross margin 83–88% across FY2023–25); rare-disease commercial infrastructure (YORVIPATH in 35+ countries, SKYTROFA >20,000 patients since launch); platform monetization beyond own sales (Novo Nordisk license, Teijin Japan royalties up to mid-20s %, Eyconis milestones/royalties).
- AGAINST: no demonstrated returns on capital (OE negative 0/5 years, negative book equity, ROIC not measurable through a cycle); single-product concentration (YORVIPATH ~80% of Q2 2026 product revenue, €252M of €315M); competition on both lead products (eneboparatide in Phase 3 for hypoparathyroidism; Sogroya and NGENLA weekly-GH rivals); SBC €116.2M in FY2025 exceeding FY2025 FCF, share count up from 56,287,060 (FY2023) to 60,607,131 (FY2025) in the EPS note; finite patent/exclusivity horizons and rare-disease pricing politics.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection. (Moot for the score — see DCF.)

## DCF — Tier F: no scenario table exists, and that is the finding
The engine's Tier F branch fired: the normalized base is not positive, so no scenarios, IVs, or IRRs are computed (implied_irr_weighted: null). Probabilities recorded for the run: 10/25/30/25/10 (defaults — nothing in the evidence justifies tilting weights for a branch that does not use them).
- **F sub-type: no_cash_generation** (f_subtype_basis: sum of the last 3 fiscal years, the median window). FCF legs from financials_history.csv: FY2023 -$519,132,315, FY2024 -$326,923,130, FY2025 +$53,359,100 — a 3-yr sum of about -$792.7M. This is not the "SBC ate positive FCF" subtype on the window as a whole, even though FY2025 alone fits that pattern (FCF +$53.4M vs SBC $136.5M).
- **Growth sanity check:** the engine's blend is 149.29% (key_numbers.md: rev CAGR 5y 150.80%, 3y 149.29%, latest YoY 123.98%). Every scenario start the engine could produce (base capped at 35%, super-bull start capped at 50%) sits far below the recent prints — FY2025 revenue +124% YoY in USD, Q2 2026 product revenue +105% YoY. Written reason, as the spec requires: those prints are a launch ramp off a near-zero base (YORVIPATH US launch August 2024) plus one-off license upfronts in the FY2023–24 revenue mix, not a steady-state growth rate — and decisively, growth applied to a negative base produces no valuation in any case. No growth input changes this tier.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 10 months ago): ttm.py was run and exits non-zero for this IFRS filer (us-gaap taxonomies only; legs unavailable) — per spec the median base is used and no TTM pin is taken. Post-FY evidence from the 2026 6-Ks is discussed under Thoughts; it does not change the scored base.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jumps): no divestiture, acquisition, or restatement — the jumps are the YORVIPATH commercial launch (EU late 2023, US August 2024) and SKYTROFA ramp, plus license upfronts inside reported revenue (Note 4: a €63.7M Teijin upfront in FY2023 revenue; a €95.3M Novo Nordisk upfront and a €27.1M non-cash Eyconis upfront in FY2024 revenue). No CAGR in the blend is trusted as a run-rate; growth inputs straddle a launch inflection, which is why the sanity check above rejects them.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2025): as filed (EUR), net loss €228,034k vs OCF +€53,897k. The cash-flow statement shows why: finance expenses of €206,687k are reversed as largely non-cash (fair-value remeasurement of financial liabilities — the Q3 2025 release alone attributed a €47.2M non-cash remeasurement loss to a single quarter), SBC of €116,171k and depreciation of €17,206k are added back, finance income of €113,999k is reversed out, and provisions added €77,585k of working capital. Net income is polluted by mark-to-market finance items that scale with the share price; the OCF-based conservative OE is the right series — and it is still negative after SBC.
- **FX_CONVERTED**: EUR reporting converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (recorded in dcf_numbers.json: 1.105 for 2023, 1.0389 for 2024, 1.175 for 2025); flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average — a screening simplification, noted.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED**: ratio 1.0 from the filer's own 20-F cover — per-share figures needed no scaling to be comparable to the traded price. See OVERRIDES.
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (2018–2022 history on non-diluted counts): fired on the filed data; the shares_override then replaced the fallback in every year 2018–2025 with the FY2025 EPS-note count. Consequence: pre-2023 per-share history uses a larger denominator than those years' own counts, so historical OE/share magnitudes are understated while the sign is unaffected. In the gated last-3-FY window the override count is within 7.7% of the filer's own per-year counts.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex** and **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:shares**: see OVERRIDES — gap, filing source, and measured impact (-$7.21 → -$7.03 on the base) are all recorded in judgment.json, dcf_numbers.json (overrides_applied / override_impact), key_numbers.md, and the central overrides registry.

## My thoughts / overlay
- There is no method range to hide behind here: zero-fill base -$7.21/share, override base -$7.03/share, latest-year-only -$1.37/share, TTM not computable for this IFRS filer. Every defensible variant is Tier F. Anyone quoting a DCF value for ASND today is projecting the inflection, not measuring owner's earnings.
- The inflection itself is real on the top line: H1 2026 revenue €585.9M in the Q2 2026 6-K (vs €259.0M H1 2025), Q2 product revenue €315M (+105% YoY; YORVIPATH €252M), Q2 non-IFRS operating profit +€92M, and management guiding FY2026 operating cash flow above €500M. But the same 6-K's IFRS profit is flattered by items that are not owner's earnings — a €158M priority-review-voucher sale in Q2 and a €654M income-tax credit in H1 — and non-IFRS profit excludes the SBC this screen counts as a real cost. The 2028 convertible notes were converted into equity in 2026 (per Q2 reporting), which cuts the debt leg but adds shares.
- What would change the tier: a filed year in which OCF − capex − SBC is positive. On management's own OCF guide that is plausible for FY2026 on a latest-year basis; the 3-yr median needs more than one such year. The FY2026 20-F (expected Feb 2027) is the refresh trigger — if its latest-year OE prints positive, this name deserves an immediate re-score rather than waiting for the queue.
- Quality note for the file: gross margin ~87% and a first positive OCF year are genuine franchise evidence; SBC at €116–136M a year against that OCF is the whole ballgame on this screen. If SBC merely flattened while OCF follows the guide, the F flips quickly — that convexity is exactly what a $225.25 price (13.7B market cap) is already paying for, with no margin of safety measurable in OE terms.

## Data / enrichment notes
- Enrichment (step 9) all ran: fundamentals.json, prices.json, segments.json, statements.json, profile.json + street.json written. Non-blocking warnings: profile.py found no extractable company description or headcount sentence in the FY2025 20-F (both fields null in profile.json); segments.py notes a 20-F filer has no 10-Qs, so quarterly segment tables are unavailable. reprice.py skipped ASND by design — Tier F names have no IRR to reprice (no live.json).

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (tier by numbers F, sub-type no_cash_generation; no tier override)
- Confidence: **Low** (high on the filed OE history — it is negative under every variant; low on how fast the 2026 inflection converts to owner's earnings)
- One-liner: Real TransCon platform with three approved rare-disease products and ~87% gross margins, moat 5/10 — but owner's earnings are negative in all of the last 5 years (normalized base -$7.03/share with the filing overrides applied; FY2025 still -$1.37/share because SBC of $136.5M exceeded FCF of $53.4M) — Tier F on this screen; it does not clear 15% at any price on current numbers and no hurdle-clearing price is computed on a negative base. The 2026 inflection (H1 revenue €585.9M, non-IFRS profit positive) is a re-rating story, not yet an owner's-earnings story.
